title: RBI issues Amendment Directions on 'Standardised Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)’
summary: The Reserve Bank of India had issued draft Amendment Directions on the ' Standardised Approach for Counterparty Credit Risk (SA-CCR)' on June 10, 2026 , inviting feedback from stakeholders until July 1, 2026. The draft Amendment Directions proposed modifications to the instructions on capital charge for counterparty credit risk as provided in Master Direction on Forthcoming Instructions for commercial banks. MSTCLTD.why_it_matters: This reaches the company indirectly via its geography, regulation exposure to SEBI, and India. The parts of the business most likely touched are revenue, demand, regulation. Classified as guidance.

ai_analysis.cost_effect: Operating costs, specifically finance and hedging costs (such as forex forward contracts used for import trading), could increase if commercial banks pass on higher capital charges resulting from the revised SA-CCR framework to their corporate clients.
ai_analysis.competitive_effect: Minimal direct impact on competitive positioning, as the RBI regulations apply system-wide to all Indian banks and will affect all trading and procurement competitors utilizing similar banking channels.
ai_analysis.regulatory_effect: No direct regulatory or compliance consequences for MSTC, as the SA-CCR guidelines apply strictly to banking institutions regulated by the RBI.
ai_analysis.short_term: Over the next 0-3 months, MSTC is unlikely to experience any material impact as banks assess the guidelines and transition to the amended SA-CCR framework.
ai_analysis.medium_long_term: Over the medium to long term, MSTC may see adjustments in the pricing of treasury and hedging products (like forex derivatives for scrap and coal imports) and trade finance facilities (LCs and BGs) depending on how banks recalibrate their capital allocation.
ai_analysis.second_order_effects: If the revised norms lead banks to tighten credit or increase the cost of bank guarantees, MSTC's auction buyers and bidders might face liquidity constraints, potentially reducing bidding volumes or participation rates on MSTC's e-commerce platforms.
ai_analysis.key_uncertainty: Whether the RBI's SA-CCR amendments will result in a net increase or decrease in capital requirements for the specific derivative and trade finance instruments that MSTC and its clients utilize.
monitor_next: Changes in MSTC's finance costs and hedging expenses in upcoming quarterly financial reports.
